jobs.description:
PRODUCT OPERATIONS & SUPPORT ASSOCIATE
ABOUT LATENT
Latent is the enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform, powered by a clinical agentic engine, that enables health systems to grow their pharmacy operations and serve more patients. One engine works across the pharmacy journey to identify patients who qualify for care, improve medication access, capture eligible prescriptions and support patients throughout treatment.
Latent’s platform enables more than 60+ leading health systems that collectively serve an estimated 70 million people. Founded by Sri Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, Latent has raised $80 million from Transformation Capital, Spark Capital, Conviction, General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and others.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Product Operations & Support Associate, you will serve as a frontline member of our Customer Enablement team, delivering empathetic, efficient, and high-quality support to our users.
This is a highly visible, fast-paced role ideal for a proactive problem-solver who can manage multiple priorities, navigate technical complexity, and ensure a seamless support experience.
This role requires coverage during standard West Coast business hours. Candidates should be available to work shifts aligned with approximately 8:00 AM–6:00 PM PT, with some flexibility based on team and customer needs.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
 - Serve as the first point of contact for customer inquiries, delivering accurate, empathetic, and timely resolutions across technical and product-related issues (AI output quality, application access, authentication, error logs, etc.).
 - Manage multiple competing priorities while maintaining strong responsiveness, reliability, and accountability during support shifts.
 - Troubleshoot complex issues in partnership with cross-functional teams, escalating appropriately while ensuring a high-quality customer experience.
 - Develop and maintain deep knowledge of Latent’s products, features, and workflows.
 - Document customer interactions, issues, and feedback to support continuous product and process improvement (FAQs, knowledge base content, internal documentation).
 - Own tasks independently while contributing to team workflows and ongoing refinement of support operations.
WHAT YOU BRING
 - 2+ years of experience in a customer support or product operations role, ideally in a high-tech or fast-paced environment.
 - Availability to consistently support customers during core Eastern and Central time zone business hours.
 - Exceptional empathy and a genuine desire to help customers succeed.
 - Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to navigate ambiguity and technical complexity.
 - Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
 - Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex concepts simply.
WHO YOU ARE
 - Deeply customer-centric with a passion for service
 - Ownership-driven with a bias toward action
 - Comfortable operating in ambiguity and adapting quickly
 - Motivated by improving healthcare at scale
WHY LATENT HEALTH
 - Mission-driven team tackling one of healthcare’s biggest challenges
 - High-ownership culture with meaningful growth opportunities
 - Competitive compensation, equity, and benefits
 - Work alongside leading experts in AI, healthcare, and product innovation

jobs.description:
About Cents
Cents is a New York-based technology company building the leading platform for the $40+ billion laundry and dry cleaning industry, helping laundromats, dry cleaners, and garment care businesses start, manage, and grow. We're backed by top-tier investors including Bessemer, Camber Creek, and Sumeru Equity Partners, and we were just ranked No. 101 on the Inc 5000 for 2026. Our team is full of passionate technology experts obsessed with supporting and empowering small business owners, and we're just getting started. If you want to help elevate an entire industry, this is where that happens.
Benefits Overview 
We offer great compensation packages, and comprehensive health benefits, & believe in a strong cohesive team atmosphere. Our laundry stipend, gym stipend and access to learning opportunities from our team and network of advisors, and investors are just the starting point! 
Equity Options 
Unlimited PTO and 12 Paid Holidays
Gym, Laundry and Work-from-home/Commuter stipend
Parental leave – Up to 14 weeks fully paid for new parents
Health benefits, including medical, dental, vision, mental health support, parental leave, life and AD&D insurance, and disability
401(k)
Cents is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital or familial status, pregnancy or pregnancy-related conditions, military or veteran status, citizenship or immigration status, arrest or conviction record, domestic violence victim status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
What You'll Do 
 Cents' Product and Engineering teams build the tools thousands of operators run their stores on every day. The Product Operations Manager runs the operating model that connects Product, Engineering, Support and Customer Success, so operator issues reach the right owner fast, launches happen cleanly across every function, engineering time goes to work that is ready to build, and leadership can see whether execution is healthy. You know the product and the data well enough to size a problem and give Engineering what they need to act, and your value is the view across the whole product organization rather than any one squad. You will report to our Director of Product Operations and work directly with product leadership.
 Own intake and triage for product and technical issues from Support and Customer Success: size the impact (stores affected, surface, workaround), route each issue to the right Product or Engineering owner, and track it to resolution against our bug SLAs.
 Lead the hotfix vs. warm fix recommendation on urgent production issues, and make sure post-incident action items land in a sprint and close.
 Coordinate release readiness for urgent fixes: make sure each has a clear owner, track required reviews, testing and approvals, confirm testing happened before deployment, and raise release risks early to the people who make the release call.
 Run the operating cadence across Product and Engineering squads (sprint kickoffs, standups, check-ins and retros), keeping decisions, risks and dependencies visible across teams. Surface dependency and capacity conflicts before commitments slip, and raise timeline risk early with a recommendation.
 Make sure work is ready before it is built: drive open questions on PRDs and acceptance criteria to closure, flag gaps before work enters a sprint, and fix the recurring gaps that cause rework.
 Partner with Product, Engineering, Support and Customer Success leaders to find recurring friction and fix the process behind it, including with AI-assisted triage and automation. Build lightweight processes and retire the ones that no longer earn their place.
 Be accountable for faster resolution of customer-impacting issues, less rework and predictable delivery, with a weekly view of execution health that leadership uses to make decisions.
What You Bring 
 5+ years of experience in product operations, program management or delivery management, ideally at a B2B SaaS startup
 Experience coordinating work across several product and engineering teams, working hands-on with engineers
 Comfort with Jira or similar tools, and an AI-native approach: you use AI in your own work today
 A self-starter who finds the work without waiting for direction and stays effective when priorities change week to week
 Sound judgment under pressure, including knowing when to escalate and when to hold
 Clear, concise writing and speaking with Product, Engineering and go-to-market teams; your summary is the one leadership forwards
 Able to work East Coast hours
Nice to Have 
 Experience with SMB customers, vertical SaaS, payments, or the laundry and dry-cleaning industry
 SQL or analytics experience (not required; our data team covers deeper analysis)
 Experience helping a team move from reactive firefighting to a measured operating model

Clēnera is a tier-one developer and independent power producer located in Boise, Idaho, and is the U.S. subsidiary of Enlight Renewable Energy (Nasdaq: ENLT ). We develop, finance, construct, own, and operate utility-scale solar and energy storage facilities throughout the United States. In its 2025 analysis of solar independent power producers, S&P Global ranked Clēnera as a top ten U.S. owner of planned installations in the next five years. Clēnera has over 1.9 GW of solar and 5.1 GWh of storage in operations or construction, and a development pipeline totaling 17.8 GW of solar and 51.1 GWh of storage across 23 states. Our company culture is at the core of everything we do, so you’ll regularly find Caring, Committed, and Courageous individuals who value respectful, cross-functional collaboration with partners internally and externally. With our tremendous portfolio growth, we are increasing our headcount to meet the demands of the business. Are you ready to change the world with us? 
 ABOUT THE ROLE 
 The Project Manager independently leads 2-4 complex construction projects, setting the execution strategy, proactively managing schedule and budget risks, and driving cross-functional accountability to meet contractual and compliance requirements. You will serve as the primary owner representative for delivery performance, stakeholder alignment, change control, and successful commissioning and turnover.

 Own execution readiness by validating scope, drawings, specifications, contract requirements, and project controls are established, and ensuring project documentation standards are implemented and sustained in Procore.

 Manage project financial performance by owning CAPEX/EPC budget tracking, spend curve management, cost code governance, and rigorous review of EPC billing, invoices, and supporting documentation to support accurate payment recommendations.
 Execute disciplined change management by evaluating change drivers, verifying documentation, assessing schedule/cost impacts, and ensuring change orders are integrated into project baselines and payment processes.
 Coordinate quality and inspection interfaces by planning and supporting AHJ and Independent Engineer (IE) inspections, tracking outcomes, and ensuring quality assurance actions remain aligned to contract deliverables and schedule needs.
 Lead commissioning, closeout, and turnover by managing punch list completion, verifying as-builts and O&M documentation, coordinating training for operations/maintenance personnel, closing contracts/final payments, and capturing lessons learned.
 Collaborate with individual department, as well as cross-functionally with other departments within the organization.
 Maintain organizational excellence in terms of project timelines and deliverables.
 Demonstrates the Clēnera Core Values of Caring, Committed, and Courageous.
 Other duties as assigned.

 Education: Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, business, or related field experience.
 Experience:
 Minimum of 5 years of experience in construction project management, and ;
 Minimum of 2 years of experience executing utility-scale renewable energy projects.
 Technology: Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Procore, and an ability to learn company-specific software programs, tools, processes, and machines.
 Skills/Attributes:
 Advanced mastery of schedule and cost controls, including critical path analysis, recovery planning, earned value, EAC forecasting, and cash flow management.

jobs.title: Credit & Collections Project Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Credit & Collections Project Analyst reports to the Credit & Collections Project Manager and supports the execution of credit risk and collections initiatives across the agent network. This role is responsible for credit line reviews, risk analysis, office-level reporting, and project support to help reduce financial exposure, improve collections performance, and ensure consistent application of credit policy.
Key Responsibilities
Credit Line Review & Risk Analysis
 Conduct regular credit line reviews at the customer and office level, assessing utilization, exposure, payment behavior, and dispute history.
 Analyze DSO, aging, and payment trends to identify risk and recommend credit line adjustments.
 Support credit limit increases, decreases, temporary overrides, and prepay recommendations with data-driven analysis.
 Identify early warning indicators of deteriorating credit performance and escalate findings to the Credit & Collections Project Manager.
 Maintain accurate documentation of credit line decisions and supporting analysis.
 Credit & Collections Analysis
 Analyze collections performance, including past-due balances, aging buckets, and recovery trends.
 Support resolution of high-risk or aged accounts through reporting and insight.
 Assist with portfolio segmentation and risk assessment initiatives.
 Office-Level & Agent Reporting Support
 Prepare office-level credit and collections reports for agent office reviews.
 Identify trends, outliers, and recurring issues across agent offices.
 Track and report follow-up actions identified during office-level reviews.
 Support materials and insights for agent conversations led by the Project Manager.
 Reporting & Dashboards
 Prepare and maintain reports and dashboards for credit line utilization, DSO, aging, exposure, and high-risk accounts.
 Ensure data accuracy, consistency, and timeliness across all reporting.
 Support ad hoc analysis requests from the Credit & Collections Project Manager.
 Project Support & Process Improvement
 Support credit and collections projects related to policy updates, system enhancements, and workflow improvements.
 Assist in standardizing credit line review processes and documentation.
 Identify opportunities to improve data visibility, controls, and efficiency.
 Support audits, compliance reviews, and leadership reporting as needed.

jobs.title: Manager, IT and Technology Operations
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find. 
 Manager, IT & Technology Operations
 GiveWell is a research organization that identifies and funds cost-effective giving opportunities, focusing on global health and well-being. Our work is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025.
 GiveWell’s ~130 (and growing!) staff are researchers, grantmakers, and fundraisers who are technically fluent, move quickly, and adopt new tools earlier than most organizations our size. When our technology fails or slows us down, the cost isn’t just frustration, but time sacrificed finding and funding interventions that save and improve lives. We’re hiring a Manager of IT and Technology Operations who will design a support program well above the typical corporate IT experience, make informed decisions about where to invest our time and resources, and bring the entire organization along. Standard IT management isn’t enough here. We need someone who understands why GiveWell is different and builds IT that supports it.
 Why is GiveWell hiring for this position now? 
 Our technology team has grown from a small group of generalists into specialized teams. Support, devices, and service quality now need a dedicated leader. On top of that, we are at a decision point on key tools, including our MDM platform and ticketing system. We have staff in Europe without a dedicated coverage plan and no internal after-hours response program. This is a real opportunity to define what excellent IT looks like at an organization where technology delays have a direct cost to impact.
 The Role
 As Manager of IT and Technology Operations, you’ll be the person responsible for making technology work for an impact-focused team. Your team owns the devices, applications, and related tooling that work happens on. One day you are scoping a new MDM platform and the next you’re negotiating a vendor renewal or coaching a specialist through a complex escalation. You’ll lead an existing team while hiring more members, own our device and support infrastructure, and step into support work yourself when it is needed.
 Here are some of the things you’d tackle in this role:
 Lead and develop your team. You’ll manage a team ranging from early-career to senior individual contributors, setting clear expectations, coaching to a high standard, and managing performance directly. Your team is your primary lever, so their growth is one of your most important outcomes.
 Design support for how GiveWell works.  Our staff expect speed and the newest tools, and they lose real impact when they’re blocked. You’ll assess how support is delivered today, recommend the right mix of in-house and vendor support, and lead that transition.
 Make calibrated calls. You’ll decide which problems deserve your team’s energy now, which can wait, and which aren’t worth fighting for. You’ll know where to hold the line (security and donor privacy) and where flexibility is the right path.
 Build a service delivery discipline. Today, we have loose SLAs and no way to measure satisfaction. You’ll define meaningful targets, build a way to measure how support feels to the people receiving it, and manage your team against both. A typical corporate IT playbook won’t work here - we consider the support of our internal teams paramount.
 Own device and endpoint operations. Your team owns the full lifecycle for our Mac-majority fleet. You’ll set our go-forward plan for MDM, whether that means a new build, a migration, or updating what we have.
 Design coverage for a distributed team. We have offices in Oakland, Brooklyn, and London, plus remote staff distributed across North America and Europe (with more expansion to come). You’ll build coverage that works across those geographies and an after-hours incident response capability with a rotation structure and escalation paths.
 Own procurement. You’ll own the budget and forecast for hardware and core software, hold signing and renewal authority for those vendors, and negotiate contracts. You’ll make, and be accountable for, spending decisions.
 Protect our data and our donors’ trust . GiveWell has spent years building trust with donors, grantees, and employees, which is critical to sustain. You will implement and maintain access controls, device security, and data handling practices across the systems you own.
 What’s not part of this role today: Salesforce, our website, data analytics, and AI enablement sit with other teams. These will be partners of yours, but not within your scope of ownership.
 About You
 The strongest candidates will have 7+ years in IT operations, technology support, or service delivery, including 3+ years managing people. Beyond that, here’s what we’re really looking for:
 You connect IT decisions to impact. You think GiveWell is doing something special, not just “doing good”, and that matters to you personally. You can explain how a slow laptop refresh or a clunky access request turns into lost research and fundraising time, and you ensure that shapes your priorities. 
 You manage people directly and well. When it comes to feedback, you operate on the principle that clear is kind. You’ve helped people grow to a higher standard than they were held to before. You’ve also made the call when someone wasn’t the right fit. You’ll join a team that already exists and you are ready to build a strong relationship with your new staff and hire top talent. 
 You have calibrated judgment. You know what to focus on and what to let go. You can name a time you chose not to enforce a standard because the cost to users outweighed the benefit, and a time you held firm. 
 You've designed IT for tech-savvy users. You’ve built (or reshaped) a support function for people who expect a lot, not just kept the lights on and maintained the status quo. You think about support as a system to be designed, set standards for, measured against, and adapted to what your users need.
 You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical users. You can explain a tradeoff to a researcher or a fundraiser in terms that help them decide

Project Expedition, a rapidly growing travel company, is seeking a Supplier Operations Associate to join our Supplier Partnerships Team. The right candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple priorities at once. You will work closely with Tour Operators and internal teams to resolve issues, maintain product quality, and support the ongoing growth of our marketplace. This is a hands-on role that requires strong communication skills, operational thinking, and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Manage product and pricing updates across the platform

 - Coordinate product profile updates, including activations and deactivations
 - Oversee content updates such as inclusions, meeting points, and product descriptions

Support new product launches and removals
 - Coordinate with internal stakeholders to launch new products

Investigate and resolve pricing and operational issues

 - Prepare operational reports and performance updates for leadership
Support compliance and reconciliation efforts
 - Track and follow up on supplier insurance documentation requirements

 - Investigate payment disputes and reconcile discrepancies using historical pricing and booking information
 - Leverage AI to optimize and automate repetitive tasks and processes

 - Clear and effective communicator with both internal and external stakeholders
